cards.name: Default Filter Colors
cards.summary: The 20 colours of Photoshop's Photo Filter list, stored in the file as 11 Lab and 9 HSB values: Warming Filter (85), (LBA) and (81), Cooling Filter (80), (LBB) and (82), Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Blue, Violet, Magenta, Sepia, Deep Red, Deep Blue, Deep Emerald, Deep Yellow and Underwater (the match to the Photo Filter list is inferred from the names). The thumbnail is a 4 x 5 grid of PGD's photographic test plate (warm indoor light) filtered with each colour in file order at 50% density with Preserve Luminosity. On this warm photo Warming 85 and LBA give an amber-orange cast and Warming 81 a golden yellow; Cooling 80 and LBB mostly cancel the warmth to a grey-mauve, while Cooling 82 turns it yellow-olive; Red, Orange and Deep Red give salmon-to-orange casts, Magenta and Violet a pink-mauve, Yellow and Deep Yellow a bright gold, Green, Deep Emerald and Underwater olive-green, Cyan a muted grey-olive, Blue and Deep Blue only a grey-mauve, and Sepia a warm olive-brown. The differences are modest because the density is 50% and the photo is already warm. The same 20 names and values also ship as Photo Filter Colors.aco in Presets/Color Swatches (ps_preset_80, item 14) and as the last 20 entries of Legacy Swatches (ps_preset_80, item 23).

cooling a warm indoor shot (Cooling 80, LBB or 82)
quick colour-grade tint for a mood: Sepia, Deep Red, Underwater
avoid: judging a cooling or blue filter on a warm photo: at 50% density it mostly cancels the warmth, so test on a cooler image

cards.name: GIF 128 Dithered
cards.summary: Save for Web (Legacy) optimize preset for GIF with a 128-colour palette and dithering on at 88% (decoded from the .irs: format code 0, colour count 128, dither flag 1, amount 88; the flag that is 1 in all GIF and PNG presets, probably Transparency, is on). Dithering scatters pixels of nearby palette colours to fake the missing in-between colours, so gradients band less at the cost of a larger file and some speckle. It is the same file as GIF 128 No Dither apart from the dither bytes, and the GIF 32, 64 and 128 presets differ from each other only in the colour-count and dither bytes.

flat logos: dithering only adds speckle, so take the No Dither twin
modern web work: Save for Web (Legacy) is the old export dialog, so for current sites export with Export As and pick the format there
